summary: The High-Capacity Grid Act requires public electric utilities to use the best-available transmission conductors for certain interstate power line projects in order to recover their costs from consumers. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission must issue regulations establishing this standard and presume that using these specific conductors is prudent while using other conductors is not prudent, with specific exemptions for emergencies, safety issues, significant unjustified costs, or projects that already have permits or materials.

affected_groups.effect: Must use best-available transmission conductors for new or majorly modified interstate transmission projects and meet new filing requirements to recover costs.
Electric bills will reflect costs recovered by utilities based on whether they used the mandated best-available transmission conductors.
Must establish a methodology, designate the conductor class, issue regulations, and evaluate cost-recovery filings and presumptions.

key_provisions: Requires public electric utilities to use best-available transmission conductors for covered interstate transmission projects.
Directs the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to issue regulations within one year in consultation with the Secretary of Energy.
Establishes legal presumptions that using best-available conductors is prudent and costs are just and reasonable, while using other conductors is not prudent.

Provides exemptions from the requirement for emergency repairs, safety or reliability conflicts, projects with significant cost increases without commensurate benefits, and projects that already filed for permits or procured conductors prior to enactment.
Applies to new transmission facility construction and major modifications, upgrades, replacements, or reconductoring of existing transmission lines.
missing_information: The specific technical criteria or metrics the Commission will use to designate the best-available transmission conductor class before the regulations are finalized.
The exact financial impact on consumer electric bills across different regions.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The High-Capacity Grid Act requires public electric utilities to use the best-available transmission conductors for certain interstate power line projects in order to recover their costs from consumers. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission must issue regulations establishing this standard and presume that using these specific conductors is prudent while using other conductors is not prudent, with specific exemptions for emergencies, safety issues, significant unjustified costs, or projects that already have permits or materials.
summary_detail.significance: This bill sets a federal standard for electric transmission lines by linking cost recovery directly to the use of high-capacity and high-efficiency conductors, impacting how utilities plan, build, and upgrade interstate power infrastructure.
